question_text: How many senators does each state have?

why_it_matters.text: Two senators is the magic number. One could die or be sick, leaving a state unrepresented. Three or more would have made the Senate huge and unwieldy. Two means each state always has someone in the chamber — and an equal voice with every other state.

fun_fact.text: Two senators per state is one of the only things in the Constitution that can never be changed by amendment. Article V says no state can be 'deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate' without its own consent. Translation: Wyoming will have exactly two senators forever, no matter how big or small it grows.
